previous_statement: Finite additivity of sums gives sum_l (max(-x(l),0)+max(-y(l),0)) = sum_l max(-x(l),0) + sum_l max(-y(l),0); by the definition of n, these three sums are n(x+y), n(x), and n(y), respectively.
new_statement: Finite additivity and the definition of n identify the inequality in node 1.3.1 as n(x+y) <= n(x)+n(y): the left side sum_l max(-(x+y)(l),0) is n(x+y), while sum_l (max(-x(l),0)+max(-y(l),0)) equals sum_l max(-x(l),0)+sum_l max(-y(l),0)=n(x)+n(y).
